newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tribasa adds partners for natgas bid.
newsitem.headline: Tribasa adds partners for natgas bid.

text.p: A Grupo Tribasa executive said Thursday the company formed a consortium with U.S.-based PNM Group, a privately held company, and Grupo Chihuahua, a group of local investors, to bid for natural gas distribution in the northern border state of Chihuahua.

"If we win the bidding we promise to invest between $80 and $100 million during the first five years to comply with the condition to reach 100,000 users," Tribasa operations vice-president Fernando Gutierrez Ochoa told Reuters.
As part of the privatization of natural gas distribution, Mexico is opening the region encompassing the cities of Chihuahua, Cuauhtemoc-Anahuac and Delicias to private investment.
Tribasa is one of at least six companies that have expressed interest in bidding for the 12-year concession in the region. Bids are due by Jan. 23, with a decision scheduled for March 20.

Gutierrez said Tribasa also is interested in bidding for operation of the Pacifico-Norte railway, which is expected to be set on the block in February. He said the company plans to incorporate a new partner in addition to RailTex Inc and Itisa.
The building company is also planning to participate in drilling and construction projects for state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), Gutierrez said.
